author: reek
body: An all-pairs gravitational N-body simulation as a [Device] compute kernel. One GPU thread owns one body; each frame it loops over ALL the other bodies, reads their positions from the shared state buffer, and sums a softened gravitational pull -- the classic O(N^2) N-body kernel. This is the reference site's "N-body simulation" technique, generated from Codex [Device] AST.

author: reek
body: The per-body force is a tail-recursive fold over the body index that reads the state buffer inside the loop: nb-fx / nb-fy take the buffer as a parameter and device-load from it (act-bound, because device-load is an effect). The WGSL plug lowers each act-block fold to a `loop` whose buffer parameter is a `ptr<storage, array<i32>, read_write>`, and the kernel passes `&<buffer>` at the call site -- the storage-pointer helper-parameter feature that also unlocks neighbour boids.

author: reek
body: One thread per body: read own state from inb, sum the pull from every body, integrate ballistically (vacuum -- no drag) with a velocity clamp for numerical stability, wrap toroidally, write outb.
